purpose: Close Chapter 2 as a public-data study linking Azami-scale spatial breadth to EAzami-scale phylogenetic depth without conflating association, historical correspondence and adaptation.

programme_roles.Azami: breadth: broad present-day spatial diversity and trait-environment structure from public images, occurrences and environmental layers
programme_roles.EAzami: depth: topology-conditioned minimum histories, relative event-depth and phylogeny-aware ecological correspondence from public phylogenomic and occurrence data
programme_roles.Chapter_2_joint_estimand: whether independently estimated spatial and phylogenetic-temporal patterns point in compatible ecological directions, and exactly where current public-data explanation stops

primary_trait_environment_questions.spatial_candidate: orientation versus precipitation amount / wetness in Azami
primary_trait_environment_questions.temporal_candidate: orientation versus CHELSA BIO15 precipitation seasonality in EAzami
required_disambiguation: estimate BIO12 annual precipitation and BIO15 precipitation seasonality on the same EAzami panels
fit BIO15 adjusted for BIO12 and BIO12 adjusted for BIO15
repeat across concatenated UFBoot topologies, complete public locus-tree topologies, ASTRAL and occurrence-source panels
do not call amount and seasonality replications unless their estimands and signs are explicitly aligned

primary_trait_environment_questions.spatial_candidate: public-image colour versus solar exposure in Azami
primary_trait_environment_questions.temporal_candidate: phylogeny-aware colour versus flowering-season solar exposure in EAzami
required_disambiguation: separate CIELAB lightness, chroma and pigment direction rather than treating colour as one category
prefer flowering-season shortwave radiation and UV exposure to annual means
retain image source, camera/background and within-taxon colour variation controls
do not discretize sparse colour data to manufacture a fourth completed history

orientation: rain-event intensity or wet-day frequency where public data are reproducibly joinable
wind exposure as a modifier of rain interception
colour: UV-B or biologically effective UV where a public source and licence are reproducible
elevation and cloudiness as correlated exposure axes

cross_scale_classes.multiscale_concordant: same trait, commensurable environmental estimand and direction are retained in both spatial and phylogeny-aware analyses
cross_scale_classes.domain_concordant_axis_distinct: both analyses implicate the same broad ecological domain but use non-equivalent axes such as precipitation amount versus seasonality
cross_scale_classes.scale_specific: a supported relationship occurs at only one scale despite evaluability at both
cross_scale_classes.unresolved: directions are estimable but uncertainty, source definition or covariance geometry prevents a stable classification
cross_scale_classes.not_evaluable: the required trait x environment x phylogeny overlap is absent

adaptation_claim_ladder.name: multiscale ecological correspondence
adaptation_claim_ladder.allowed: compatible spatial and phylogeny-aware directions; consistent with adaptive differentiation

adaptation_claim_ladder.name: event-specific ecological correspondence
adaptation_claim_ladder.allowed: repeated transition-bearing lineages align with independently reconstructed exposure shifts, with uncertainty propagated

adaptation_claim_ladder.name: adaptive function
adaptation_claim_ladder.allowed: requires independent functional or fitness evidence and is outside a public comparative analysis alone

public_data_saturation_definition: All currently machine-reusable, source-auditable datasets in the frozen registry are queried under outcome-independent taxonomic, coordinate, thinning, phenology and trait-quality rules. This is not a literal claim that every webpage or unpublished observation has been exhausted.
claim_boundaries: A spatial Azami coefficient and a phylogenetic EAzami coefficient are not pooled as statistical replicates.
BIO12 amount and BIO15 seasonality are related precipitation dimensions but not the same estimand.
Concordance across scales can motivate adaptive hypotheses but does not by itself establish selection or fitness benefit.
Present-day niche centroids are not ancestral environments or dated transition events.
Sparse taxon-level colour summaries must retain within-taxon variation and source uncertainty.
A significant sensitivity tier cannot replace the frozen primary solely because it crosses P<0.05.
